Subject: Salesforce - Unable to create opportunities, error 'UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW'
Description: Sales team unable to create new opportunities in Salesforce. When attempting to save a new opportunity, users receive error message: 'UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW: unable to obtain exclusive access to this record or 1 record'. Resolution Notes: CRITICAL INCIDENT - Salesforce opportunity creation resolved: 1) Accessed Salesforce as admin and replicated the issue - confirmed UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW error. 2) Checked Setup > Apex Jobs > Scheduled Jobs - discovered a custom batch job 'OpportunityScoreUpdate' running since 9:15 AM that was locked, processing records. 3) Examined debug logs - batch job was updating all 45,000+ opportunity records simultaneously to recalculate scoring, causing row locks. 4) Identified that job was scheduled to run monthly but had been mistakenly triggered manually this morning by junior admin during testing. 5) Immediately aborted the running batch job via Developer Console: System.abortJob('707xx00000xxxxx'). 6) Verified all record locks released by querying AsyncApexJob object. 7) Tested opportunity creation - successful save in 2 seconds. 8) Had 3 sales users test creating new opportunities - all successful. 9) Rescheduled OpportunityScoreUpdate batch job to run during off-hours (2 AM) with reduced batch size (200 records per batch instead of 5000) to prevent future locking issues. 10) Modified batch job governor to check for business hours before execution. 11) Created monitoring alert to detect long-running batch jobs during business hours. 12) Updated admin procedures to prevent manual batch job execution during peak times. 13) Documented incident in change log and sent notification to sales team that system fully operational. Total downtime: 47 minutes. Backlog of 23 opportunities created successfully in following hour. Recommended: Implement row-level locking strategy review for all batch processes.
Infra System: Salesforce Platform (Row Locking / Apex Batch Jobs)

Subject: SAP - Finance posting failed, period 12/2025 is closed for posting

discovered posting period was closed at 11:47 PM last night by user 'SAP_BATCH' (automated job user). 3) Investigated scheduled background jobs via SM37 - identified job 'MONTH_END_AUTO_CLOSE' that ran last night at 11:45 PM. 4) Job was scheduled to close period 11/2025 (November) but incorrectly closed period 12/2025 (December) due to parameter error in variant configuration. 5) Current status and actions taken: a) Confirmed this is NOT a correct period close - December should remain open for 2 more days. b) Immediately opened emergency change request ticket with CFO approval for period reopening. c) Contacted SAP Basis team leader for authorization - security protocol requires two-person approval for period reopening. 6) Waiting for: a) CFO written approval via email (received 9:15 AM - approved). b) SAP Basis security officer approval (pending - manager currently in meeting, expected within 30 minutes). c) Change Advisory Board emergency approval (submitted request at 9:20 AM). 7) Prepared remediation steps ready to execute upon approval: a) Execute transaction OB52 to reopen period 12/2025 for all account types in company code 1000. b) Verify period authorization settings for all affected account types (A-Assets, D-Customers, K-Vendors, M-Materials, S-G/L). c) Test posting with sample journal entry to confirm period is functional. d) Notify finance team that posting is restored. e) Disable automated job 'MONTH_END_AUTO_CLOSE' until job parameters can be corrected. f) Implement additional approval step in job scheduler for any period-closing jobs. 8) Root cause analysis in parallel: a) Job variant 'Z_CLOSE_VAR_001' contains hardcoded period value '12' that should have been '11'. b) Job was created 6 months ago and has been closing wrong periods but went unnoticed as periods were reopened manually. c) No validation logic exists in job to confirm correct period before execution. 9) Temporary workaround: Finance team redirected to post to held document status (transaction FB01 with HOLD flag) so entries are ready for immediate posting once period reopened. Customer orders are being accepted on website but not reaching warehouse - no order confirmations being sent to customers. Revenue impact: Approximately $287,000 in orders pending processing. Warehouse team unaware of orders and cannot begin picking/shipping. Error message in Boomi logs: 'Connection timeout to SAP RFC destination'. SAP system is operational (verified by logging in directly). Network connectivity between Boomi and SAP tested successfully. Integration was processing normally yesterday - last successful order sync: Yesterday 11:58 PM, 847 orders processed. Boomi environment: Production (atom-prod-01), Process: Shopify_to_SAP_Orders_v2.3.
Resolution Notes: CRITICAL - E-commerce integration restored: 1) Logged into Boomi AtomSphere console, navigated to Process Reporting. 2) Examined failed execution logs for 'Shopify_to_SAP_Orders' - all showing same error at SAP connection step: 'RFC_ERROR_SYSTEM_FAILURE: Connection attempt timed out after 30 seconds'. 3) Checked Boomi Atom server status (atom-prod-01) - server running normally, CPU 23%, memory 45%, network responsive. 4) Tested connectivity to SAP directly from Boomi atom server using SAP logon - connection successful, indicating network path is functional. 5) Root cause identified: Reviewed SAP system logs (SM21) - discovered SAP gateway service 'sapgw00' on application server 'sap-prd-01' had crashed at 6:45 AM (2 minutes before integration failures began). Gateway crash caused by memory leak in custom SAP RFC function module 'Z_ECOM_ORDER_CREATE'. 6) Immediate resolution: a) Restarted SAP gateway service on application server: Logged into SAP via SSH, executed command: 'sudo systemctl restart sap-gateway-PRD-00'. b) Verified gateway service running: 'systemctl status sap-gateway-PRD-00' - Status: Active (running). c) Tested RFC connection from Boomi - successful connection established. 7) Reprocessed failed orders: a) In Boomi AtomSphere, selected all 523 failed process executions. b) Used 'Resubmit' function to re-execute failed orders. c) Monitored execution in real-time - orders processing successfully at rate of ~12 per minute. d) All 523 orders processed successfully within 48 minutes (completed at 10:35 AM). 8) Verified in SAP: Logged into SAP transaction VA05 (List of Sales Orders) - confirmed all 523 orders created with correct customer data, line items, pricing, delivery addresses. Orders automatically released to warehouse management system. 9) Customer notification: E-commerce team triggered manual order confirmation emails for all 523 affected customers (normally automatic via integration). 10) Fixed underlying SAP issue: a) Analyzed RFC function module 'Z_ECOM_ORDER_CREATE' code - identified memory leak: internal table 'lt_order_items' not being cleared in loop processing. b) Applied code fix: Added 'CLEAR lt_order_items' statement at end of each loop iteration. c) Transported code fix to production after testing in development environment. d) Restarted SAP application server to clear any residual memory issues. 11) Enhanced monitoring: a) Configured SAP gateway monitoring alert in SAP Solution Manager to detect service failures within 2 minutes. b) Added Boomi process monitoring alert for execution error rate >5% to trigger immediate notification. c) Implemented heartbeat monitoring: Scheduled test order every 30 minutes to verify end-to-end integration health. 12) Warehouse impact mitigation: Contacted warehouse manager - all 523 orders now visible in WMS. Authorized overtime staffing (10 additional pickers) for afternoon shift to process backlog. Estimated catch-up time: 6 hours. All orders will ship today. 13) Financial impact: Revenue of $287,000 preserved (all orders will fulfill). No order cancellations. Total integration downtime: 3 hours 48 minutes. Average order delay: 4 hours (acceptable given same-day shipping cutoff at 4 PM). Executive summary sent to CEO and COO. Recommended: Conduct full RFC performance audit for all custom functions handling high-volume transactions. Incident post-mortem scheduled for Thursday.

Subject: Boomi - Customer data sync delayed, CRM records out of sync with ERP
Description: Sales team reporting that customer information in Salesforce CRM is not matching data in SAP ERP system. Specifically, customer addresses, phone numbers, and credit limits are outdated in Salesforce. Integration process 'SAP_to_Salesforce_Customer_Sync' normally runs every 2 hours to sync master data changes. Last successful run was 18 hours ago (yesterday 4 PM). Subsequent scheduled runs showing 'Completed' status in Boomi but no data is actually updating in Salesforce. Verified by comparing test customer record: SAP shows updated address from yesterday 5 PM, Salesforce still shows old address. Affecting sales team's ability to quote correctly - credit limits are critical for large order approvals. IT received 8 tickets from sales reps about data discrepancies. Boomi environment: Production (atom-prod-02), Process: SAP_to_SF_Customer_Master_v1.8. No recent changes to integration process. Both SAP and Salesforce systems individually accessible and operational.
Resolution Notes: Investigation in progress - data sync troubleshooting: 1) Logged into Boomi AtomSphere, reviewed SAP_to_Salesforce_Customer_Sync process executions from last 24 hours. 2) Examined execution logs - 9 scheduled runs showing Completed status but with unexpected log entry: 0 records retrieved from SAP for processing. This explains why Salesforce not updating. 3) Tested SAP connection manually using Boomi Test mode - manual test also returns 0 records, issue is in SAP data retrieval. 4) Logged into SAP to investigate custom function module Z_GET_CUSTOMER_DELTA - discovered anomaly: Last sync timestamp shows future date 2026-01-20 (6 days from now). 5) Root cause: Timestamp corruption in sync log table. Function module comparing records against future timestamp, resulting in 0 records. 6) Future timestamp was written yesterday at 4:37 PM during SAP Basis daylight saving time adjustment script - script added 6 days instead of 6 hours due to parameter error. 7) Corrective action: Update ZCUST_SYNC_LOG table to correct timestamp. Created transport request, submitted emergency change to CAB at 10:15 AM. 8) Prepared remediation plan ready to execute once approved. 9) Impact: 34 customer records with changes not reflected in Salesforce (12 address updates, 8 phone changes, 7 credit limit adjustments, 5 contact updates, 2 payment terms). 10) Temporary workaround: Sales Operations manually updating high-priority records for active deals. 11) Preventive measures: Add validation logic to reject future timestamps, implement monitoring alert for 0 records condition, review SAP Basis scripts. Next steps: Awaiting CAB approval (ETA 12 noon), then 30-minute fix window. Current workaround in place. Priority MEDIUM. Estimated resolution: 3-4 hours.
Infra System: Boomi + SAP Delta Extract + Salesforce Sync
